expectations.text: Distinguishes between full disk and mmap
expectations.evidence: Section 'Why full disk mode was so slow' explains: 'each hop in the graph is a random disk read... Multiply that by hundreds of hops and you get your 3-4 second latency.' Mmap explained in section 1: 'the OS manages a page cache. Vectors live on disk but frequently accessed pages stay in the OS page cache (RAM).'

expectations.text: Recommends mmap as the middle ground
expectations.evidence: Opening states 'there is absolutely a middle ground.' Section 1 recommends mmap for vectors. Section 2 titled 'Keep the HNSW index in RAM, put vectors on disk' is described as 'the most common middle ground configuration and likely what you want.'

Section 3 Scalar Quantization code example includes 'always_ram=True'. Explains: 'keep quantized vectors in RAM' while full vectors live on disk for rescoring. Recommended config point 3: 'Quantization: scalar (INT8) with always_ram=True'.

Multiple latency estimates: 'Expected latency: 15-50ms' for scalar quantization, '20-100ms range' for HNSW in RAM + vectors on disk, '15-60ms search latency' for recommended config. All well under 500ms.

expectations.text: Does NOT recommend going back to full RAM
expectations.evidence: The response does not recommend reverting to full RAM. It presents the middle ground as the recommended approach. The recommended configuration uses on-disk vectors with quantization, stating it gives '~75-85% memory reduction compared to full RAM' with '15-60ms search latency.'
